subject.title: Bound batch file read with size cap in config-set-input

question: Should `openclaw config set --batch-file` adopt an unconditional 8 MiB maximum, and if so what compatibility and user-facing failure contract should apply to existing larger batch files?
rationale: The code can enforce any selected limit, but neither source evidence nor the discussion establishes that rejecting previously accepted public CLI input above 8 MiB is an intended product and upgrade policy.

options.title: Approve a documented 8 MiB limit
options.body: Accept the runtime rejection contract, document the size limit and error behavior, and add focused upgrade/compatibility coverage.

options.title: Choose a compatibility-preserving bound
options.body: Keep the hardening but select an owner-approved capacity and behavior that avoids unexpectedly breaking established batch automation.

options.title: Defer the cap
options.body: Keep the current unrestricted compatibility contract until a supported batch-input limit can be designed and communicated.

recommendation.title: Choose a compatibility-preserving bound
recommendation.body: Keep the hardening but select an owner-approved capacity and behavior that avoids unexpectedly breaking established batch automation.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied timeline identifies them as the only human review-routing signal attached to the earlier required decision.
